AGENCY:
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), DOT.
ACTION:
Notice of proposed special conditions.
SUMMARY:
This action proposes special conditions for the Embraer S.A. (Embraer) Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane. This airplane will have a novel or unusual design feature when compared to the state of technology envisioned in the airworthiness standards for transport category airplanes. This design feature is a functionality known as the Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System (E
2
TS). The applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for this design feature. These proposed special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.
DATES:
Send comments on or before November 27, 2026.

and follow the online instructions for sending your comments electronically.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Comments Invited
The FAA invites interested people to take part in this rulemaking by sending written comments, data, or views. The most helpful comments reference a specific portion of the proposed special conditions, explain the reason for any recommended change, and include supporting data.
The FAA will consider all comments received by the closing date for comments, and will consider comments filed late if it is possible to do so without incurring delay. The FAA may change these special conditions based on the comments received.
Privacy
Except for Confidential Business Information (CBI) as described in the following paragraph, and other information as described in
title 14, Code of Federal Regulations
(14 CFR) 11.35, the FAA will post all comments received without change to
www.regulations.gov
,
including any personal information you provide. The FAA will also post a report summarizing each substantive verbal contact received about these special conditions.
Confidential Business Information
Confidential Business Information (CBI) is commercial or financial information that is both customarily and actually treated as private by its owner. Under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (
5 U.S.C. 552
), CBI is exempt from public disclosure. If your comments responsive to these special conditions contain commercial or financial information that is customarily treated as private, that you actually treat as private, and that is relevant or responsive to these special conditions, it is important that you clearly designate the submitted comments as CBI. Please mark each page of your submission containing CBI as “PROPIN.” The FAA will treat such marked submissions as confidential under the FOIA, and the indicated comments will not be placed in the public docket of these proposed special conditions. Send submissions containing CBI to the individual listed in the For Further Information Contact section above. Comments the FAA receives, which are not specifically designated as CBI, will be placed in the public docket for these proposed special conditions.
Background
On December 5, 2021, Embraer applied for a change to Type Certificate No. A57NM to add a functionality known as E
2
TS in the Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane. The Embraer Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane is a twin-engine, transport category airplane with a maximum passenger capacity of 146, and a maximum takeoff weight of 135,584 pounds.
Type Certification Basis
Under the provisions of
14 CFR 21.101
, Embraer must show that the changes to the Embraer Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane continue to meet the applicable provisions of the regulations listed in Type Certificate No. A57NM or the applicable regulations in effect on the date of application for the change, except for earlier amendments as agreed upon by the FAA.
If the Administrator finds that the applicable airworthiness regulations (
e.g.,
14 CFR part 25
) do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for the Embraer Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane because of a novel or unusual design feature, special conditions are prescribed under the provisions of § 21.16.
Special conditions are initially applicable to the model for which they are issued. Should the type certificate
(
printed page 67531)
for that model be amended later to include any other model that incorporates the same novel or unusual design feature, or should any other model already included on the same type certificate be modified to incorporate the same novel or unusual design feature, these special conditions would also apply to the other model under § 21.101.
In addition to the applicable airworthiness regulations and special conditions, the Embraer Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane must comply with the exhaust emission requirements of
14 CFR part 34
, and the noise-certification requirements of
14 CFR part 36
.
The FAA issues special conditions, as defined in
14 CFR 11.19
, in accordance with
14 CFR 11.38
, and they become part of the type certification basis under § 21.101.
Novel or Unusual Design Features
The Embraer Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane will incorporate the following novel or unusual design feature:
The Embraer ERJ 190-400 airplane will have a functionality known as Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System (E
2
TS), a function which automatically controls the airplane's pitch and bank angle without pilot input to the airplane controls.
Discussion
E
2
TS is an autoflight function specifically designed to improve takeoff performance and enhance operational safety. It is engaged at the beginning of the takeoff roll, when the thrust levers are advanced to the takeoff go-around (TOGA) detent. Upon engagement, the airplane control in pitch—including the takeoff rotation maneuver and initial climb-out—will be automatically performed, without any pilot intervention. Control of the bank angle will also be automatically performed by E
2
TS, maintaining wings level while the airplane is on the ground and the directional tracking when the airplane is in the air. During the ground run, the flight crew is responsible for maintaining runway centerline via manual directional control, with augmentation provided by the E
2
TS to minimize heading deviations.
Once the airplane is airborne, E
2
TS provides control using sideslip as the reference. If all engines are operating (AEO), zero sideslip is the reference; if one engine is inoperative (OEI), then the Best Beta is considered as the sideslip reference. It is noted that any flight crew intervention on the rudder pedal is summed with the rudder controls that are output by the E
2
TS mode.
Takeoff performance requirements of
14 CFR part 25
require the ability to safely complete the takeoff or bring the airplane to a complete stop in a rejected takeoff. As written, the takeoff performance requirements presuppose manual flying with a human pilot onboard making certain decisions and taking action. In fact, paragraph 4.4.5.1 of AC 25-7D reads: “The rotation speed, V
R
, is intended to be the speed at which the pilot initiates action to raise the nose wheel(s) off the ground during the acceleration to V
2
.” The current regulations do not take into consideration that the takeoff rotation is being performed by an automatic system, not a human being.
These special conditions specifically address paragraphs 25.107(e)(3) and (e)(4), which deal with human pilot variability effects in flying the airplane (formerly called “takeoff abuse tests”). That is, instead of considering the “reasonably expected variations in service” of the original rules, one should now consider “maximum expected deviations” due to sensor accuracy and system tolerances.
Furthermore, for E
2
TS operation, V
R
is the speed at which this system will perform the rotation, and the speed the pilot will use to monitor the automatic rotation. Determination of “maximum expected deviations of V
R
” should reflect “in-service” variations and may be done using a combination of analyses, simulations, and certification flight tests, including, but not limited to, performance and handling qualities tests. Such analyses will result in a deviation that should ensure a level of safety equivalent to or higher than operational flights with conventional takeoffs (manual takeoff with pilot in the loop).
Lastly, to ensure consistency between flight test demonstrations and actual, in-service operations, compliance with
14 CFR 25.101
must be shown, especially paragraphs 25.101(d), (e), (f), and (h).
When demonstrating compliance with these special conditions, the following guidance applies:
The FAA understands that the automatic rotation provided by E
2
TS function is expected to reduce rotation variabilities as human piloting variabilities will not be present. Paragraph 25.107(e)(1)(iv) requires an airplane “maximum practicable rate” rotation maneuver. However, sensor inaccuracies and system tolerances will still be present and should be considered as residual variabilities. These residual variabilities should be evaluated in the operational envelope (considering weight, CG, thrust, altitude, temperature, and wind) in a manner that the V
LOF
/V
MU
required margins from 25.107(e)(1)(iv) can be met considering the maximum expected deviations on V
LOF
.
Any demonstrations required to show compliance to these special conditions should consider the operational envelope (
i.e.,
weight, CG, thrust, altitude, temperature, and winds) in a manner that the required margins on Airplane Flight Manual (AFM) takeoff distance can be met considering the maximum expected deviations. Performance testing should be executed in limited wind conditions and calculations should assume no wind gusts. Wind gusts need not be considered in demonstrations for compliance with these special conditions.
The proposed special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.
Applicability
As discussed above, these proposed special conditions are applicable to the model for which they are issued. Should the type certificate for that model be amended later to include any other model that incorporates the same novel or unusual design feature, or should any other model already included on the same type certificate be modified to incorporate the same novel or unusual design feature, these special conditions would apply to the other model as well.
Conclusion
This action affects only a certain novel or unusual design feature on one model of airplanes. It is not a rule of general applicability.

14 CFR Part 25
Aircraft
Aviation safety
Reporting and recordkeeping requirements
Authority Citation
The authority citation for these special conditions is as follows:
Authority:
49 U.S.C. 106(f)
,
40113
,
44701
,
44702
, and
44704
.
The Proposed Special Conditions
Accordingly, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposes the following special conditions as part of the type certification basis for Embraer Model ERJ 190-400 series airplanes.
(a) In lieu of compliance with 25.107(e)(3), for automatic takeoff systems, the one-engine inoperative takeoff distance, accounting for the maximum expected deviation of V
R
allowed by E
2
TS, must not exceed the
(
printed page 67532)
corresponding AFM takeoff distance established in accordance with § 25.113(a)(1).
(b) In lieu of compliance with 25.107(e)(4), for automatic takeoff systems, accounting for the maximum expected deviation of V
R
allowed by E
2
TS, or in out-of-trim conditions, the all-engines-operating takeoff distance must not exceed the corresponding AFM takeoff distance, established in accordance with § 25.113(a), by more than 1%. Deviations of other parameters that might influence pitch rotation dynamics (
e.g.,
pitch angle, pitch rate) must be accounted for, unless the effect of such deviations on the takeoff distance is shown to be negligible.
(c) Operation of the E2TS function must not result in unsafe flight characteristics.

Department of Transportation

[Docket No. FMCSA-2026-3466]
AGENCY:
Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA), Department of Transportation (DOT).
ACTION:
Notice of application for exemption; request for comments.
SUMMARY:
FMCSA requests public comment on PAM Transport Inc.'s (PAM) application for an exemption from the requirement that a holder of a commercial learner's permit (CLP) who has successfully passed the commercial driver's license (CDL) skills test but not yet been issued CDL credentials be accompanied by a CDL holder in the front seat, while the commercial motor vehicle (CMV) is driven by the CLP holder. PAM states that the CDL holder would remain in the CMV while the CLP holder is driving, but not necessarily in the passenger seat of the vehicle. FMCSA is required by statute to publish a notice explaining each exemption request. This notice does not indicate what decision FMCSA will ultimately reach on the request. After reviewing the application, safety analyses, and public comments submitted, FMCSA will grant or deny the exemption.
DATES:
Comments must be received on or before November 27, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
You may submit comments identified by Docket Number FMCSA-2026-3466 by any of the following methods:
Federal eRulemaking Portal:
www.regulations.gov
.
See the Public Participation and Request for Comments section below for further information.
Mail:
Dockets Operations, U.S. Department of Transportation, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, W58-213, West Building, Washington, DC 20590-0001.
Hand Delivery or Courier:
1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, W58-213, West Building, Washington, DC 20590-0001, between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
Fax:
(202) 493-2251. Each submission must include the Agency name and the docket number (FMCSA-2026-3466) for this notice. Note that DOT posts all comments received without change to
www.regulations.gov
,
including any personal information included in a comment. Please see the Privacy Act heading below.
Privacy Act:
In accordance with
49 U.S.C. 31315(b)
, DOT solicits comments from the public to better inform its exemption process. DOT posts these comments, including any personal information the commenter provides, to
www.regulations.gov
,
as described in the system of records notice DOT/ALL-14 FDMS (Federal Docket Management System (FDMS)), which can be reviewed at
https://www.transportation.gov/​individuals/​privacy/​privacy-act-system-records-notices
.
The comments are posted without edit and are searchable by the name of the submitter.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Mr. Richard Clemente, FMCSA Driver and Carrier Operations Division; Office of Carrier, Driver and Vehicle Safety Standards;
richard.clemente@dot.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Public Participation and Request for Comments
FMCSA encourages you to participate by submitting comments and related materials.
A. Submitting Comments
If you submit a comment, please include the docket number for this notice (FMCSA-2026-3466), indicate the specific section of this document to which the comment applies, and provide a reason for your suggestions or recommendations. You may submit your comments and material online or by fax, mail, or hand delivery, but please use only one of these means. FMCSA recommends that you include your name and mailing address, an email address, or a phone number in the
(
printed page 67646)
body of your document so the Agency can contact you if it has questions regarding your submission.
To submit your comment online, go to
https://www.regulations.gov/​docket/​FMCSA-2026-3466/​document
,
click on this notice, click “Comment,” and type your comment into the text box on the following screen.
If you submit your comments by mail or hand delivery, submit them in an unbound format, no larger than 8
                    1/2
                     by 11 inches, suitable for copying and electronic filing.
FMCSA will consider all comments and material received during the comment period. Comments received after the comment closing date will be filed in the public docket and will be considered to the extent practicable.
B. Confidential Business Information (CBI)
CBI is commercial or financial information that is both customarily and actually treated as private by its owner. Under the Freedom of Information Act (
5 U.S.C. 552
), CBI is exempt from public disclosure. If your comments responsive to the notice contain commercial or financial information that is customarily treated as private, that you treat as private, and that is relevant or responsive to the notice, it is important that you clearly designate the submitted comments as CBI. Please mark each page of your submission that constitutes CBI as “PROPIN” to indicate it contains proprietary information. FMCSA will treat such marked submissions as confidential under the Freedom of Information Act, and they will not be placed in the public docket of the notice. Submissions containing CBI should be sent to Sarah Stella, Chief, Regulatory Development Division, Office of Policy, FMCSA, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590-0001 or via email at
sarah.stella@dot.gov
.
At this time, you need not send a duplicate hardcopy of your electronic CBI submissions to FMCSA headquarters. Any comments FMCSA receives not specifically designated as CBI will be placed in the public docket for this notice.
C. Viewing Comments and Documents
To view comments, as well as any documents mentioned in this preamble as being available in the docket, go to
https://www.regulations.gov
,
insert FMCSA-2026-3466 in the keyword box, select the document tab and choose the document to review. To view comments, click this notice, then click “Browse Comments.” If you do not have access to the internet, you may view the docket by visiting Dockets Operations in the DOT West Building, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, W58-213, Washington, DC 20590-0001, between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
II. Legal Basis
FMCSA has authority under
49 U.S.C. 31136(e)
and
31315(b)
to grant exemptions from the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSRs). FMCSA must publish a notice of each exemption request in the
Federal Register
(
49 CFR 381.315(a)
). The Agency must provide the public an opportunity to inspect the information relevant to the application, including the applicant's safety analysis. The Agency must provide an opportunity for public comment on the request.
The Agency reviews the application, safety analyses, and public comments submitted and determines whether granting the exemption would likely achieve a level of safety equivalent to, or greater than, the level that would be achieved absent such exemption, pursuant to the standard set forth in
49 U.S.C. 31315(b)(1)
. The Agency must publish its decision in the
Federal Register
(
49 CFR 381.315(b)
). If granted, the notice will identify the regulatory provision(s) from which the exempted party will be exempt, the effective period, and all terms and conditions of the exemption (
49 CFR 381.315(c)(1)
). If the exemption is denied, the notice will explain the reason for the denial (
49 CFR 381.315(c)(2)
). The exemption may be renewed (
49 CFR 381.300(b)
).
III. Applicant's Request
Current Regulatory Requirements
The Agency's CDL regulations in
49 CFR 383.25(a)(1)
require that a CLP holder always be accompanied by the holder of a valid CDL for the group (
e.g.,
Group A or B) and with any endorsement(s) necessary to operate the CMV. The CDL holder must be physically present in the front seat of the vehicle next to the CLP holder or, in the case of a passenger vehicle, directly behind or in the first row behind the driver and must have the CLP holder under observation and direct supervision.
Applicant's Request
PAM recruits and develops entry-level commercial drivers through partnerships with CDL training programs, including programs where training is conducted in a State other than the driver's State of domicile. The applicant seeks a 5-year exemption from the provisions in
49 CFR 383.25(a)(1)
to allow CLP holders who have successfully passed a CDL skills test and are thus eligible to receive a CDL to drive a CMV without a CDL holder present in the front passenger seat of the vehicle. PAM states that the exemption, if granted, would allow the CLP holder to begin employment in a timelier manner, strengthen their newly acquired driving skills, and participate in a revenue-generating trip back to their State of domicile to obtain their CDL documents.
PAM estimates that approximately 500-700 CLP holders would operate each year under the terms of the exemption. Absent the exemption, PAM states that the driver's transition into productive employment would be delayed until the driver's State of domicile issues the CDL or the driver is sent home in a non-driving capacity. The applicant asserts that this outcome is inefficient for PAM and presents a lost employment opportunity for the driver. PAM states that the administrative waiting period results in operational inefficiencies and financial hardships for already-trained drivers, and the potential degradation of recently acquired driving skills. PAM further adds that as the trucking industry is already experiencing significant driver turnover, requiring drivers to remain idle during this period may increase attrition and discourage workforce participation.
Applicant's Equivalent Level of Safety
PAM asserts that exemption will result in a level of safety that is equivalent to, or greater than, the level of safety without the exemption, as it would limit CMV operation under the exemption to drivers who have passed the CDL skills test and therefore have demonstrated that they meet stringent qualification requirements. Before a driver may operate under the exemption, PAM would verify that the driver: (1) holds a valid CLP issued by the driver's State of domicile; (2) holds a valid State-issued driver's license from the jurisdiction that issued the CLP; (3) has successfully completed the applicable CDL skills examination and possesses evidence of this completion; (4) holds all endorsements required for the CMV being operated; (5) is medically qualified to operate the CMV; (6) is not subject to an out-of-service order or suspension of driving privileges; (7) satisfies PAM's driver qualification requirements; and (8) has a qualified CDL holder with the appropriate CDL class and endorsements physically present in the CMV while the CLP holder is operating the CMV under the exemption. PAM would also require the driver to
(
printed page 67647)
maintain possession of the required documentation, including a valid State driver's license, valid CLP, documentation demonstrating successful completion of the CDL skills test, and a copy of the FMCSA exemption, and ensure that these documents are accessible in the event of an inspection by authorized Federal, State, or local enforcement officials. PAM would document operations under the exemption and continuously monitor the safety performance of the CLP holder and adds that any driver who becomes ineligible under the conditions of the exemption would be immediately removed from operation under the exemption.
A copy of PAM's application for exemption is available for review in the docket for this notice.
IV. Request for Comments
In accordance with
49 U.S.C. 31315(b)
, FMCSA requests public comment from all interested persons on PAM's application for an exemption from the requirement that a CLP holder be accompanied by a CDL holder with the proper CDL class seated in the front seat while the CLP holder operates the CMV. All comments received before the close of business on the comment closing date will be considered and will be available for examination in the docket at the location listed under the Addresses section of this notice. Comments received after the comment closing date will be filed in the public docket and will be considered to the extent practicable. In addition to late comments, FMCSA will also continue to file, in the public docket, relevant information that becomes available after the comment closing date. Interested persons should continue to examine the public docket for new material.

Associate Administrator for Policy.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Technology description follows:
Compositions and Methods for Detecting Lymphatic Filariasis
Description of Technology
Lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis; LF) is a neglected tropical disease characterized by painful deformation of the host. LF affects over 120 million people throughout the tropics and subtropics of Asia, Africa, the Western Pacific, and parts of the Caribbean and South America. LF results from infection with the filarial parasites
Wuchereria bancrofti
or
Brugia malayi.
Current methods of confirming active
(
printed page 67594)
infection by
W. bancrofti
or
B. malayi
include microscopy and immunoassays using serum/plasma extracted from the patient. However, the sensitivity of microscopy detection varies among patients, and existing immunoassays show cross-reactivity with antibodies directed towards other parasites, such as
Onchocerca volvulus
or
Loa loa,
whose geographic distribution can overlap with the LF-causing filarial parasites.
This new technology addresses the limitation of cross-reactivity, presenting an opportunity for a directed assay towards the detection of
W. bancrofti
or
B. malayi.
Preliminary data against sera from LF-affected individuals indicates Wb4 is effective at detecting
B. malayi.
Wb4B, a modified version of recombinant Wb4 that lacks the nineteen (19) amino acid signal sequence of full-length Wb4, appears capable of isolation and purification by traditional molecular biology techniques and shows improved response in immunoassays.
The subject technology, including the antigen sequence for Wb4B and plasmids enabling bacterial, insect, and mammalian cell expression, is available for licensing for commercial development in accordance with
35 U.S.C. 209
and
37 CFR part 404
, as well as for further development and evaluation under a research collaboration.
There may be the potential to combine this technology with other NIAID-developed biomarker technologies (Wb123, available for licensing, HHS Ref. No. E-281-2010-0, “Diagnostic Assays and Methods of Use for Detection of Filarial Infection” and Wb5, available for licensing, HHS Ref. No. E-093-2022-0, “Compositions and Methods for Detecting Lymphatic Filariasis”) for the development of a multiplex assay for detection of active
W. bancrofti
or
B. malayi
infection for diagnostic or surveillance purposes.
Potential Commercial Applications:
Diagnostics for
W. bancrofti
and
B. malayi
infection.
Surveillance for
W. bancrofti
and
B. malayi
prevalence.
Competitive Advantages:
Increased specificity compared to available diagnostics.
Differentiation from other parasites with similar geographic footprints.
Development Stage:
Pre-Clinical.

Dr. Thomas B. Nutman and Dr. Sasisekhar Bennuru, both of NIAID.

SUMMARY:
The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. Model SA226-T, SA226-AT, SA226-T(B), SA226-TC, SA227-AC (C-26A), SA227-AT, SA227-BC (C-26A), SA227-PC, SA227-CC, SA227-DC (C-26B), and SA227-TT (300) airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of in-flight pitch trim actuator failures. This AD requires repetitively inspecting the pitch trim actuator for cracked, missing, or compromised sealant, replacing and sealing the pitch trim actuator if cracked, missing, or compromised, repetitively measuring the pitch trim actuator travel time, and depending on the results of the measurements, replacing and sealing the pitch trim actuator. This AD also requires certain pitch trim actuators to be sealed after installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
DATES:
This AD is effective December 1, 2026.
The Director of the Federal Register approved the incorporation by reference of certain publications listed in this AD as of December 1, 2026.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
The FAA issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) to amend
14 CFR part 39
by adding an AD that would apply to certain Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. Model SA226-T, SA226-AT, SA226-T(B), SA226-TC, SA227-AC (C-26A), SA227-AT, SA227-BC (C-26A), SA227-PC, SA227-CC, SA227-DC (C-26B), and SA227-TT (300) airplanes. The NPRM was published in the
Federal Register
on April 2, 2026 (
91 FR 16595
). The NPRM was prompted by reports of in-flight pitch trim actuator failures. In the NPRM, the FAA proposed to require repetitively inspecting the pitch trim actuator for cracked, missing, or compromised sealant, replacing and sealing the pitch trim actuator if the sealant is found cracked, missing, or compromised, repetitively measuring the pitch trim actuator travel time, and depending on the results of the measurements, replacing and sealing the pitch trim actuator. The proposed AD would prohibit the installation of certain pitch trim actuators unless the pitch trim actuator is sealed.
The FAA is issuing this AD to prevent moisture intrusion into the pitch trim actuator body through the rod end keyway and pitch trim actuator piston. The unsafe condition, if not addressed, could result in pitch trim actuator failure and reduced control of the airplane.
The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
Discussion of Final Airworthiness Directive
Comments
The FAA received comments from two commenters. The commenters were Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. and World Class Accessory, Inc. The commenters requested changes to the proposed service information, compliance requirements, and installation provisions. The following presents the comments received on the NPRM and the FAA's response to each comment.
Request To Incorporate the Latest Revisions of the Service Information
Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. requested that the latest revisions of the service bulletins be incorporated into the NPRM: Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. SA227 Service Bulletin (SB) 227-27-067R3 dated March 2, 2026, and Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. SA226 Service Bulletin 226-27-087R3 dated March 2, 2026.
The FAA agrees. The latest revisions clarify the repetitive travel time measurements for the different actuators, update manpower requirements, and align the allowable system voltage for the actuator time travel measurements for the DL5040M5, Mod 1 actuator. None of these changes substantively affect the required actions for operators but instead are clarifying. This AD has been revised to incorporate the latest revisions of the applicable service bulletins while retaining credit for actions accomplished before the effective date of this AD using the service bulletin revisions referenced in the NPRM.
(
printed page 67436)
Request To Revise Paragraph (h) Required Actions for Model Group 1 Airplanes
World Class Accessory, Inc. requested editorial changes to the Required Actions for Model Group 1 Airplanes in paragraphs (h)(2) and (3) of the proposed AD. The commenter requested changing the phrase “seal the pitch trim actuator in accordance with” to “seal the pitch trim actuator rod ends in accordance with” for clarification.
The FAA disagrees. The FAA reviewed the requested editorial changes and determined that a revision is not necessary. The language in this AD is consistent with the service information from the design approval holder (DAH). The FAA did not change this AD as a result of this comment.
Request To Maintain the Repetitive Measurement Interval
Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. requested that the repetitive measurement interval for airplanes equipped with an originally installed Simmonds-Precision pitch trim actuator, part number DL5040M5, remain identical by maintaining the current interval of not to exceed 250 flight hours or 6 calendar months, whichever occurs first.
The FAA agrees. This AD has the repetitive measurement intervals for both Group 1 and Group 2 airplanes equipped with an original DL5040M5 pitch trim actuator at intervals of not to exceed 250 flight hours or 6 calendar months, whichever occurs first. These intervals were selected to align with the repetitive inspection intervals required by AD 2007-16-03, Amendment 39-15142 (
72 FR 43139
, August 3, 2007) (AD 2007-16-03), and the DAH service information. Operators should already be accomplishing these repetitive inspections at the established intervals; therefore, this AD can be done at already established maintenance activity. The FAA did not change this AD as a result of this comment.
Request To Require Accomplishment by a Repair Station
World Class Accessory, Inc. requested revising paragraph (h)(1) of the proposed AD to require that the inspection of the ram of each actuator be accomplished only by a repair station. The commenter stated that the inspection cannot be accomplished in the field.
The FAA disagrees. The applicable Ontic service bulletins provide the information necessary to accomplish the required actions. It is the owner/operator's responsibility to ensure that those actions are performed by a qualified and licensed mechanic per FAA regulations. The FAA did not change this AD as a result of this comment.
Request To Revise the Installation Prohibition
World Class Accessory, Inc. requested revising the installation prohibition because the pitch trim actuator (PTA) rod ends cannot be sealed until the actuator is installed on the airplane, adjusted, and rigged. The commenter stated that the rod ends must be adjusted, secured, and sealed after installation on the airplane before the actuator can be returned to service.
The FAA agrees with the intent of the comment. The FAA acknowledges that the PTA must be installed on the airplane before sealant can be applied to the rod ends. However, the FAA disagrees that the installation prohibition prevents compliance with the AD. The return-to-service procedures in the applicable Ontic service bulletins account for this step. Specifically, Step 2.C.1.a of the Ontic service bulletin instructs maintenance personnel to apply sealant to each ram rod end in accordance with Step 2.B.8 after the actuator is installed on the airplane and rigging/adjustment is complete. The actuator must be sealed before the airplane is returned to service. The FAA revised paragraph (j) of this AD to clarify the installation prohibition language to ensure the return to service procedures in the applicable service bulletins are followed.
Changes Since the NPRM Was Issued
In Table 1 of paragraph (h)(5)(ii), the NPRM was missing a row for Simmonds-Precision pitch trim actuator P/N DL5040M8. The FAA has corrected the table in this final rule.
Conclusion
The FAA reviewed the relevant data, considered any comments received, and determined that air safety requires adopting this AD as proposed. Accordingly, the FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. Except for minor editorial changes, and any other changes described previously, this AD is adopted as proposed in the NPRM. None of the changes will increase the economic burden on any operator.
Material Incorporated by Reference Under
1 CFR Part 51

SA227 Service Bulletin 227-27-067R3, dated March 2, 2026; and Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. SA226 Service Bulletin 226-27-087R3, dated March 2, 2026. This material specifies procedures for inspections and functional checks of the pitch trim actuator and measurement of the pitch trim actuator travel time. These documents are distinct because they apply to different airplane models. This material is reasonably available because the interested parties have access to it through their normal course of business or by the means identified in the

Although the material specifies to submit certain information to the manufacturer, this AD does not include that requirement.

Authority for This Rulemaking
Title 49 of the United States Code specifies the FAA's authority to issue rules on aviation safety. Subtitle I, section 106, describes the authority of the FAA Administrator. Subtitle VII: Aviation Programs, describes in more detail the scope of the Agency's authority.
The FAA is issuing this rulemaking under the authority described in Subtitle VII, Part A, Subpart III, Section 44701: General requirements. Under that section, Congress charges the FAA with promoting safe flight of civil aircraft in air commerce by prescribing regulations for practices, methods, and procedures the Administrator finds necessary for safety in air commerce. This regulation is within the scope of that authority because it addresses an unsafe condition that is likely to exist or develop on products identified in this rulemaking action.

2026-21-13 Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. (Type Certificate Previously Held by Swearingen, Fairchild Aircraft, and M7 Aerospace):
Amendment 39-23502; Docket No. FAA-2026-2723; Project Identifier AD-2024-00429-A.
(a) Effective Date
This airworthiness directive (AD) is effective December 1, 2026.
(b) Affected ADs
None.
(c) Applicability
This AD applies to Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. (type certificate previously held by Swearingen, Fairchild Aircraft, and M7 Aerospace) model and serial number airplanes, certificated in any category, as identified in paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this AD.
(1) Group 1 airplanes: Model SA226-T, SA226-AT, SA226-T(B), SA226-TC, SA227-AC (C-26A), SA227-AT, SA227-BC (C-26A), SA227-PC, and SA227-TT (300) airplanes, all serial numbers with a pitch trim actuator Simmonds-Precision part number (P/N) DL5040M5, DL5040M6, or DL5040M8 installed.
(2) Group 2 airplanes: Model SA227-CC and SA227-DC (C-26B), all serial numbers with a pitch trim actuator Simmonds-Precision P/N DL5040M5, DL5040M6, or DL5040M8 installed.
(d) Subject
Joint Aircraft System Component (JASC) Code 2731, Elevator Tab Control System.
(e) Unsafe Condition
This AD was prompted by reports of in-flight pitch trim actuator failure. The FAA is issuing this AD to prevent moisture intrusion into the pitch trim actuator body through the rod end keyway and pitch trim actuator piston. The unsafe condition, if not addressed, could result in pitch trim actuator failure and reduced control of the airplane.
(f) Compliance
Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
(g) Definitions
For the purpose of this AD:
(1) A new part is a pitch trim actuator with zero-hours time-in-service (TIS).
(2) An overhauled part is a pitch trim actuator that has zero hours TIS since the last overhaul.
(h) Required Actions for Model Group 1 Airplanes
(1) For all affected airplanes, at whichever compliance time in paragraph (h)(1)(i) or (ii) of this AD occurs later, inspect the ram of each actuator, specifically the pitch trim actuator rod ends, to determine if the sealant is cracked, missing, or compromised in accordance with Step 2.B.7, of the Accomplishment Instructions in Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. SA227 Service Bulletin (SB) 227-27-067R3 dated March 2, 2026, (Ontic SB 227-27-067R3) or Ontic Engineering and Manufacturing, Inc. SA226 Service Bulletin 226-27-087R3 dated March 2, 2026, (Ontic SB 226-27-087R3), as applicable for your airplane.
(i) Within 1,000 flight hours or 6 calendar months since the pitch trim actuator was put into service, whichever occurs first; or
(ii) Within 30 days after the effective date of this AD.
(2) For affected airplanes with any pitch trim actuator whose rod ends have been found to have cracked, missing, or compromised sealant per the inspection in paragraph (h)(1) of this AD, and have at least 1,000 flight hours or at least 6 calendar months, whichever is less since the pitch trim actuator was put into service, before further flight, replace the pitch trim actuator with a new or overhauled pitch trim actuator and install and seal the pitch trim actuator in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, Step 2.B.8, Ontic SB 227-27-067R3 or Ontic SB 226-27-087R3, as applicable for your airplane.
(3) For affected airplanes with any pitch trim actuator whose rod ends have been found to have cracked, missing, or compromised sealant per the inspection in paragraph (h)(1) of this AD, and have less than 1,000 flight hours or 6 calendar months, whichever is less since the pitch trim actuator was put into service, before further flight, inspect and apply sealant to the pitch
(
printed page 67438)
trim actuator in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, Step 2.B., of Ontic SB 227-27-067R3 or Ontic SB 226-27-087R3, as applicable for your airplane.
(4) For all affected airplanes, repetitively inspect and seal the pitch trim actuator every 1,000 flight hours or every 12 calendar months, whichever occurs first, after the inspection required in paragraph (h)(1), in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, Step 2.B., Ontic SB 227-27-067R3 or Ontic SB 226-27-087R3, as applicable for your airplane.
(5) For all affected airplanes, at whichever compliance time in paragraph (h)(1)(i) or (ii) of this AD occurs later, measure the pitch trim actuator travel time in accordance with the Accomplishment Instructions, Step 2.A., Ontic SB 227-27-067R3 or Ontic SB 226-27-087R3, as applicable for your airplane.
(i) If either pitch trim actuator rod does not meet travel time criteria, before further flight, replace the pitch trim actuator with a new or overhauled pitch trim actuator.
(ii) If both pitch trim actuator rods meet travel time criteria, repeat the measurement of the pitch trim actuator at intervals specified below in table 1 to paragraph (h)(5)(ii) of this AD.

AGENCY:
Department of Defense (DoD).
ACTION:
Establishment of Federal Advisory committee.
SUMMARY:
The DoD (referred to herein as “the Department of War” or “DoW”) is publishing this notice to announce it is establishing the Advisory Council on Health and Human Performance Optimization (“the Council”) as a discretionary Federal advisory committee.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Jim Freeman, Advisory Committee Management Officer for the DoW, 703-692-5952.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
In August 2026 and in accordance with authority described in
Chapter 10 of Title 5 United States Code
(U.S.C.) 1008(a)(2), the Secretary of War (SecWar) approved the establishment of the Council. The public or interested organizations may submit written statements about the Council's mission and functions.
The Council will operate in accordance with
chapter 10 of title 5, U.S.C.
(“commonly known as the Federal Advisory Committee Act” or “FACA”), and 41 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) part 102-3, “Federal Advisory Committee Management,” [90
Federal Register
58417; December 16, 2025], and DoW policies and procedures.
Written statements may be submitted at any time or in response to the stated agenda of planned meetings of the Council. All written statements shall be submitted to the Council Designated Federal Officer (DFO), CAPT Shawn Clausen, U.S. Navy, 703-275-6060, or
shawn.s.clausen.mil@health.mil
.
The DFO will ensure all written statements are provided to the membership for their consideration. Consistent with
41 CFR 102-3.65(a)
, the DoW is publishing the Council's Public Interest Determination.
Pursuant to
41 CFR 102-3.60(a)
, to establish, renew, reestablish, or merge a discretionary (agency discretion) advisory committee, an agency must first consult with the General Services Administration's Committee Management Secretariat (the Secretariat) and, as part of the consultation, provide a written public interest determination approved by the head of the agency to the Secretariat with a copy to the Office of Management and Budget. In addition, pursuant to
41 CFR 102-3.35
, an agency shall follow the same consultation process and document in writing the same determination of need before creating a subcommittee under a discretionary committee that is not made up entirely of members of a parent advisory committee.
Information on the following factors for the Council is provided to the Secretariat to demonstrate that establishing the Council is in the public interest:
1.
Annual Budget:
The DoW estimates annual operating costs to support the Council are $1,368,170, which includes personnel travel, meetings, and contract support.
a.
Federal personnel on a full-time equivalent basis:
The estimated annual personnel costs to the DoW are 1.5 full-time equivalent at $422,043, which includes basic pay with cost-of-living allowance.
b.
Other Federal internal costs:
$861,127.
c.
Proposed payments to members:
Consistent with
10 U.S.C. 173
, members of the Council are not compensated for their services, except for travel and per diem reimbursement for official Council-related business.
d.
Proposed number of members:
As authorized by the SecWar, the Council will be composed of not more than 20 members and subcommittees, if authorized, will be composed of not more than 15 members.
e.
Reimbursable costs:
The estimated reimbursement costs, to include travel, for Advisory Committee on Health and Human Performance Optimization staff and members are $85,000.
2.
If applicable, the total dollar value of grants expected to be recommended during the fiscal year:
N/A.
3.
Criteria for selecting members to ensure the committee has the necessary expertise and balanced membership:
As described in its proposed charter and membership balance plan, Council members will be talented, innovative private and public sector health care leaders and membership shall be drawn from individuals with expertise in any of the following disciplines:
(a) Urology/Andrology
(b) Endocrinology
(c) Nutrition
(d) Neurology/Brain Health
(e) Combat Stress Physiology/Military Operational Medicine
(f) Defense Health Agency Representative
(g) Lifestyle Medicine
(h) Preventive Medicine/Biostatistics/Epidemiology
(i) Orthopedics/Sports Medicine/Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
(j) Digital Health and Wearable Technology
(k) Psychiatry/Psychology/Spiritual Resilience
(l) Sleep Medicine
(m) Strategic Foresight and Biomedical Innovation/Human Factors Engineering
In evaluating candidates for the Council, the DoW considers education, life experience, and professional credentials concerning the subject matters anticipated to be tasked to the Council. The DoW has found that viewing the complex issues facing the DoW through a multidisciplinary advisory committee provides the DoW and, more importantly, the American public with a broader understanding of the issues on which subsequent policy decisions are based. Membership shall be fairly balanced in terms of points of view represented and the functions to be performed by the Council. The Council's membership balance is not static, and the DoW Appointing Authority may change the membership based upon work assigned to the Council.
4.
List of all other DoW Federal Advisory Committees:
A complete listing of DoW Federal advisory committees can be located at:
https://www.facadatabase.gov/​FACA/​s/​account/​001t000000DCAooAAH/​department-of-defense
.
5.
Justification that the information or advice provided by the Federal advisory committee or subcommittee is not available from another Federal advisory committee, another Federal Government source, or any other more cost-effective and less burdensome source:
The Council will serve as a high-impact, low-cost mechanism for the DoW to secure the expertise of the nation's foremost leaders at the nexus of warrior health and performance. The Council will provide knowledge derived from extensive experience with issues, techniques, and strategies that impact, optimize, and re-establish well-being and performance in the face of challenging circumstances. This expertise is essential to accelerate evaluation and potential applications of strategies to improve human performance among members of the DoW Active and Reserve Components, to maintain a ready fighting force on the leading edge of lethality, and to better care for those suffering from operational stressors and exposures.
Focused exclusively on human performance, the Council will provide the SecWar and Deputy Secretary of
(
printed page 67555)
War with a unique advisory capability specific to optimization of warfighter health and performance that is not otherwise available to the SecWar from within the Department. While other DoW advisory bodies focus broadly on strategic defense technology (
e.g.,
the Science, Technology, and Innovation Board) or standard clinical healthcare delivery (
e.g.,
the Defense Health Board), no other body is dedicated exclusively to the holistic optimization, rapid validation, and field-integration of human performance capabilities across Total Force Fitness (TFF) domains.
Securing this highly specialized, multi-disciplinary expertise through traditional federal hiring is prohibited by civil service recruiting timelines and caps. Fulfilling these requirements via commercial advisory contracts is cost-prohibitive, lacks the long-term continuity required for multi-year strategic programs, and cannot legally provide the independent, collective consensus advice authorized under FACA.
The Council represents an exceptionally cost-effective resource. Its membership will be drawn from volunteer subject matter experts who are highly specialized in human performance. Special Government Employee Members serve without compensation and receive only travel and per diem reimbursement for official council-related business. Once chartered, the Council and its subcommittees function as a standing advisory body, capable of initiating critical evaluations and reports without the delays associated with new procurements or contracts.
6.
If the consultation is a committee renewal, a summary of the previous accomplishments of the committee and the reasons it needs to continue:
N/A.
7.
Explanation of why the committee/subcommittee is essential to the conduct of agency business:
The Council directly advances the Administration's core national security priorities by providing independent advice and recommendations ensuring America's warfighters' physical attributes fully align with the goal of deterring adversaries through strength—not weakness—by producing lethal, operationally ready warriors prepared physically, psychologically, for successful large-scale, high kinetic, combat operations against peer adversaries who are imbued with the essential Warrior Ethos to win decisively. The American people have entrusted the DoW and its Commanders with the Nation's most vital asset—the American Warfighter. The Commissioned and Non-Commissioned Officers leading Soldiers, Sailors, Airmen, Marines, and Guardians hold direct responsibility for the physical fitness, mental acuity, and combat focus of their teams. The modern battlefield demands physiologic resilience while operational stress impacts performance, recovery, and physiological health. The DoW maintains weapon systems and equipment with precision, discipline, and accountability, yet does not currently manage Warfighter performance with that same level of rigor. That gap directly impacts readiness, increases operational risk, and limits warrior lethality and effectiveness. Warfighter Performance Optimization (WPO) is the Department's approach to closing this gap. By building on and modernizing the principles of TFF, WPO will provide leaders with the data, tools, capabilities, and resources required to understand Warfighter performance, anticipate degradation, and take necessary actions. WPO will deliver a unified operational approach to accelerate readiness, dominance, and peak performance across the Force. The DoW treats the Warfighter as a readiness capability, held to the same disciplined evaluation, maintenance, and optimization the DoW demands of every asset that preserves combat power, optimizes performance, combats Operator Syndrome, and maximizes mission readiness to achieve total victory on any battlefield anywhere and anytime.
A component to WPO is alleviating the impact of allostatic load—the cumulative wear-and-tear on the Warrior's body from repeated exposure to stress. Many military occupations require constant readiness, prolonged separation from family, high-stakes decision-making, physical and psychological trauma, and repeated exposure to danger, often over decades. WPO and TFF work together to prevent, identify and manage combat and operational stress issues as early as possible, before they become medical problems. The Council's advice and recommendations will serve to support WPO initiatives on Warrior physiological and psychological maintenance, longevity, mobility/flexibility and stress mitigation, preparing American Warfighters to better able to handle the rigors and stress of the job in a military career.
The Council's advice and recommendations will allow the DoW to create, manage, and sustain a rapid pipeline to identify, validate, and scale innovations and capabilities that give our warfighting teams a decisive edge. This means aggressively fielding data analytics, wearables, and cutting-edge technologies across modernized TFF domains that improve performance in demanding operational environments, not just in a lab.
The Council efforts will provide a critical component in advancing the DoW's essential core business of restoring the warrior ethos, rebuilding our military and reestablishing deterrence with its focus on building and maintaining a ready, lethal fighting force prepared to dominate all aspects of battlespace and achieve peace through strength.

ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
The National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics within the National Science Foundation (NSF) is announcing plans to request renewal of the Survey of Earned Doctorates (OMB Control Number 3145-0019) . In accordance with the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, we are providing opportunity for public comment on this action. After obtaining and considering public comments, NCSES will prepare the submission requesting OMB clearance of this collection for three years.
DATES:
Written comments on this notice must be received by December 28, 2026 to be assured consideration. Comments received after that date will be considered to the extent practicable. Send comments to the address below.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Suzanne H. Plimpton, Reports Clearance Officer, U.S. National Science Foundation, Randolph Building, 401 Dulany Street, Alexandria, Virginia 22314; telephone (703) 292-7556; or send email to
splimpto@nsf.gov
.
Individuals who use a telecommunications device for the deaf (TDD) may call the Federal Information Relay Service (FIRS) at 1-800-877-8339, which is accessible 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year (including Federal holidays).
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Title of Collection:
Survey of Earned Doctorates.
OMB Control Number:
3145-0019.
Expiration Date of Current Approval:
June 30, 2028.
Type of Request:
Intent to seek approval to renew information collection for three years.
Abstract:
Established within the NSF by the America COMPETES Reauthorization Act of 2010 section 505, codified in the NSF Act of 1950, as amended, the National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics (NCSES) serves as a central Federal clearinghouse for the collection, interpretation, analysis, and dissemination of objective data on science, engineering, technology, and research and development for use by practitioners, researchers, policymakers, and the public.
The Survey of Earned Doctorates (SED) is part of NCSES' portfolio and collects data on individuals to provide information on science and engineering education and careers in the United States. The SED has been conducted annually since 1958 and is jointly sponsored by four Federal agencies (NSF/NCSES, National Institutes of Health, U.S. Department of Education/National Center for Education Statistics, and National Endowment for the Humanities) to avoid duplication of effort in collecting such data. It is an accurate, timely source of information on our Nation's highly educated individuals. This request to renew the information collection for three years is to cover the 2028 and 2029 SED survey cycles.
Data are obtained via Web survey from each person earning a research doctorate from an accredited U.S. institution at the time they receive the degree. Data are collected on their field of specialty, educational background, sources of support in graduate school, debt level, postgraduation plans, and demographic characteristics. NCSES publishes statistics from the survey in several reports. The survey will be collected in conformance with the Privacy Act of 1974. Responses from individuals are voluntary. NCSES will ensure that all individually identifiable information collected will be kept strictly confidential and will be used only for research or statistical purposes.
Use of the Information:
The Federal Government, policy makers, universities, researchers, and others use the information extensively. Results from the SED are used to assess characteristics of the doctorate population and trends in doctoral education and degrees. Data from the survey are published annually on the NCSES website in a publication series reporting on all fields of study, titled
Doctorate Recipients from U.S. Universities
(
https://ncses.nsf.gov/​pubs/​nsf26315
). Information from the SED is also included in other series available online such as
Science and Engineering Indicators (
https://ncses.nsf.gov/​indicators
).
In addition, access to tabular data from selected variables is available through the NCSES online data tool (
https://ncsesdata.nsf.gov/​builder/​sed
) and the SED Restricted Data Analysis System (
https://ncsesdata.nsf.gov/​rdas/​#/​
).
Expected Respondents:
The SED is a census of all individuals receiving a research doctorate from an accredited U.S. academic institution in the academic year beginning July 1 and ending June 30 of the subsequent year. As such, the population for the 2028 SED consists of all individuals receiving a research doctorate in the 12-month period beginning July 1, 2027 and ending June 30, 2028. Likewise, the population for the 2029 SED consists of all individuals receiving a research doctorate in the 12-month period beginning July 1, 2028 and ending June 30, 2029. A research doctorate is a doctoral degree that (1) requires completion of an original intellectual contribution in the form of a dissertation or an equivalent culminating project (
e.g.,
musical composition) and (2) is not primarily intended as a degree for the practice of a profession. The most common research doctorate degree is the Ph.D. Recipients of professional doctoral degrees, such as MD, DDS, JD, DPharm, and PsyD, are not included in the SED. The 2028 and 2029 SED are expected to include about 615 separately reporting schools with eligible research doctoral programs from about 480 doctorate-granting institutions. Based on the historical trend, NCSES expects a stable turnout of research doctorates for the next few years with a nominal increase from the 2026 cycle estimating that approximately 62,000 individuals will receive a research doctorate from U.S. institutions in each of the 2028 cycle and the 2029 cycle.
In addition to the questionnaire for individuals receiving their research doctorates, the SED needs to collect administrative data such as graduation lists from participating academic institutions. An Institutional Coordinator at each institution helps distribute the Web survey link, track
(
printed page 67615)
survey completions, and submit information to the SED survey contractor.
Estimate of Burden:
An average overall response rate of 91.5% of the persons who earned a research doctorate from a U.S. institution was obtained in the academic years 2023, 2024, and 2025. Using the past response rate, the number of SED respondents in each cycle is estimated to be 56,730 (62,000 doctorate recipients × 0.915 response rate) in each of the 2028 and 2029 cycles.
Based on the average Web survey completion time for the 2026 SED (19.3 minutes), NCSES estimates that, on average, 20 minutes per respondent will be required to complete the 2028 or 2029 SED Web survey. The annual respondent burden for completing the SED is therefore estimated at 18,910 hours in 2028 and in 2029 (based on 56,730 respondents × 20 minutes).
Based on focus groups conducted with Institutional Coordinators, it is estimated that the SED takes no more than 1% of the Institutional Coordinator's time over the course of a year, which computes to 20 hours per year per Institutional Coordinator (40 hours per week × 50 weeks per year × .01). With 615 schools expected to participate in the SED in both 2028 and 2029, the estimated annual burden to Institutional Coordinators of administering the SED is 12,300 hours per survey cycle.
Therefore, the total burden for the SED is estimated to be 31,210 (18,910 + 12,300) hours each for the 2028 and 2029 survey cycles. NCSES estimates that the average annual burden for the 2028 and 2029 survey cycles over the course of the three-year OMB clearance period will be no more than 20,807 hours [(31,210 hours + 31,210 hours)/3 years].
Comments:
Comments are invited on (a) whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the NCSES, including whether the information shall have practical utility; (b) the accuracy of the NCSES's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information; (c) ways to enhance the quality, use, and clarity of the information on respondents, including through the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology; and (d) ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology.

AGENCY:
Food and Drug Administration, HHS.
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA, Agency, or we) has determined that PEPCID RPD (famotidine) orally disintegrating tablets, 20 milligrams (mg) and 40 mg, were not withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness. This determination will allow FDA to approve abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs) for famotidine) orally disintegrating tablets, 20 mg and 40 mg, if all other legal and regulatory requirements are met.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Heather Dorsey, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Food and Drug Administration, 10903 New Hampshire Ave., Bldg. 51, Rm. 6220, Silver Spring, MD 20993-0002, 301-796-3600,
heather.dorsey@fda.hhs.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Section 505(j) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) (
21 U.S.C. 355(j)
) allows the submission of an ANDA to market a generic version of a previously approved drug product. To obtain approval, the ANDA applicant must show, among other things, that the generic drug product: (1) has the same active ingredient(s), dosage form, route of administration, strength, conditions of use, and (with certain exceptions) labeling as the listed drug, which is a version of the drug that was previously approved, and (2) is bioequivalent to the listed drug. ANDA applicants do not have to repeat the extensive clinical testing otherwise necessary to gain approval of a new drug application (NDA).
Section 505(j)(7) of the FD&C Act requires FDA to publish a list of all approved drugs. FDA publishes this list as part of the “Approved Drug Products With Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations,” which is known generally as the “Orange Book.” Under FDA regulations, drugs are removed from the list if the Agency withdraws or suspends approval of the drug's NDA or ANDA for reasons of safety or effectiveness or if FDA determines that the listed drug was withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness (
21 CFR 314.162
).
A person may petition the Agency to determine, or the Agency may determine on its own initiative, whether a listed drug was withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness. This determination may be made at any time after the drug has been withdrawn from sale, but must be made prior to approving an ANDA that refers to the listed drug (§ 314.161 (
21 CFR 314.161
)). FDA may not approve an ANDA that does not refer to a listed drug.
PEPCID RPD (famotidine) orally disintegrating tablets, 20 mg and 40 mg, are the subject of NDA 020752, held by Merck & Co., Inc., and initially approved on May 29, 1998. PEPCID RPD is indicated for short term treatment of active duodenal ulcer, maintenance therapy for duodenal ulcer patients at reduced dosage after healing of an active ulcer, short term treatment of active benign gastric ulcer, short term treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease, and treatment of pathological hypersecretory conditions (
e.g.,
Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome, multiple endocrine adenomas).
In a letter dated September 11, 2013, Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp., (Merck) notified FDA that PEPCID RPD (famotidine) orally disintegrating tablets, 20 mg and 40 mg, were being discontinued, and FDA moved the drug product to the “Discontinued Drug Product List” section of the Orange Book. In the same letter, Merck Sharp requested withdrawal of NDA 020752 for PEPCID RPD (famotidine) orally disintegrating tablets, 20 mg and 40 mg. In the
Federal Register
of June 21, 2017 (
82 FR 28322
), FDA announced that it was withdrawing approval of NDA 020752, effective July 21, 2017.
Lachman Consultant Services, Inc. submitted a citizen petition dated June 29, 2026 (Docket No. FDA-2026-P-7178), under
21 CFR 10.30
, requesting that the Agency determine whether PEPCID RPD (famotidine) orally disintegrating tablets, 20 mg and 40 mg, were withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness.
After considering the citizen petition and reviewing Agency records and based on the information we have at this time, FDA has determined under § 314.161 that PEPCID RPD (famotidine) orally disintegrating tablets, 20 mg and 40 mg, were not withdrawn for reasons of safety or effectiveness. The petitioner has identified no data or other information suggesting that these drug products were withdrawn for reasons of safety or effectiveness. We have carefully reviewed our files for records concerning the withdrawal of PEPCID RPD (famotidine) orally disintegrating tablets, 20 mg and 40 mg, from sale. We have also independently evaluated relevant literature and data for possible postmarketing adverse events. We have reviewed the available evidence and determined that this drug product was not withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness.
Accordingly, the Agency will continue to list PEPCID RPD (famotidine) orally disintegrating tablets, 20 mg and 40 mg, in the “Discontinued Drug Product List” section of the Orange Book. The “Discontinued Drug Product List” delineates, among other items, drug products that have been discontinued from marketing for reasons other than safety or effectiveness. ANDAs that refer to these drug products may be approved by the Agency as long as they meet all other legal and regulatory requirements for the approval of ANDAs. If FDA determines that labeling for these drug products should be revised to meet current standards, the Agency will advise ANDA applicants to submit such labeling.

Notice.
SUMMARY:
The International Trade Administration (ITA) announces the launch of the U.S. Resources Management Industry Listing (RMIL), or “industry listing.” The RMIL is intended to identify U.S. companies operating in water and wastewater treatment; waste management and recycling, including critical minerals recycling; air quality measuring, monitoring and control; monitoring and instrumentation; weather and forecasting; and other resources management sectors for informational, engagement, and policy support purposes. The RMIL will provide a platform for U.S. companies to market their products and services, raising their visibility with international buyers seeking to purchase U.S. resources management solutions. The RMIL supports ITA's efforts to promote American technologies and services to overseas partners and position U.S. companies to compete for international project opportunities. Eligible companies may now apply to be listed in the RMIL. The industry listing will be published online and will be maintained by the International Trade Administration's Office of Energy and Environmental Industries.
DATES:
Applications to be listed in the RMIL are now being accepted. To be included in the initial launch, companies should submit a complete application by December 11, 2026. Applications received after that date will be accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis.
ITA anticipates launching the RMIL in February 2027 and will thereafter update the listing and add new industry profiles on a rolling basis. Only companies that submit complete applications will be considered for the listing.
ADDRESSES:
Additional information and the application form are available at
https://www.trade.gov/​us-resources-management-industry-listing-application
.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Natural Resources Team, Office of Energy and Environmental Industries, International Trade Administration; email:
envirotech@trade.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The RMIL will include manufacturers and service providers across the water and wastewater treatment, waste management and recycling, air quality measurement, monitoring and control, monitoring and instrumentation, weather and forecasting, and other resources management sectors. Together, these industries provide essential equipment, machinery, components, and services that support the buildout of critical infrastructure and enable efficient, safe, and reliable manufacturing operations. The industry provides vital support to manufacturing sectors central to U.S. economic and national security, including water purification for semiconductor manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, food and beverage, and other industrial facilities; water efficiency and water reuse technologies for data centers; recycling equipment and processes for critical minerals recovery; and industrial air purification equipment for power and heavy manufacturing. The industry contributes approximately $37 billion in U.S. goods and services exports annually and supports approximately 1.9 million American jobs.
To promote the competitiveness of the U.S. exports and U.S. companies engaged in these sectors, the International Trade Administration is developing an industry listing that catalogs eligible firms providing resources management technologies and services. The listing aims to improve U.S. companies' visibility with potential foreign partners, generate business opportunities, and advance U.S. technological leadership. Listing benefits will range from showcasing a company's unique solutions, improving visibility to foreign buyers and investors through a free and publicly accessible resource, identifying prospective business partners, and deepening engagement with ITA and other U.S. federal government agencies.
Eligible companies include U.S. entities involved in the design, engineering, manufacturing, construction, operation, maintenance, or support of resources management solutions across the below sectors:
Water and wastewater treatment;
Waste management and recycling, including critical minerals recycling;
Air quality measurement, monitoring and control;
Monitoring and instrumentation;
Weather and forecasting; and
Other resources management sectors.
Applicants will be required to certify their sector(s) of coverage in the application form to demonstrate their qualifications for listing in the RMIL.
Note:
The RMIL is intended to be a resource for U.S. exporters, manufacturers, and service providers. This listing is not comprehensive. Appearing in the RMIL does not imply endorsement or certification by the U.S. Government. The RMIL is not intended for U.S. Government procurement purposes. ITA strongly recommends RMIL users to perform their own due diligence investigation and background research on any company in the RMIL. ITA assumes no responsibility for the professional ability or integrity of the providers listed. ITA reserves the right not to list any particular company.
Selection Criteria
Eligible U.S. companies will be asked to make the following certifications in the application form in order to qualify for entry in the RMIL:
1. The company seeking listing is not majority-owned or controlled by a foreign government entity or foreign government entities;
2. The company seeking listing offers U.S. goods or services relevant to the resources management sector including water and wastewater treatment, waste management and recycling, air quality monitoring and control, monitoring and instrumentation, weather and forecasting, and other resources management sectors;
3. The goods or services of the company seeking listing are of U.S. origin or have at least 51% U.S. content by value;
4. The export of the goods, software, technology, and/or services of the company seeking listing would be undertaken in compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, including those administered by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, and U.S. sanctions laws and regulations, including those maintained by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC);
5. Neither the company seeking listing nor any of its subsidiaries or affiliates are currently listed on any OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list or other sanctions list maintained by the U.S. Government;
6. Neither the company seeking listing nor any of its subsidiaries or affiliates have been charged with, or convicted of, any civil or criminal violations of U.S.
(
printed page 67542)
export control or sanctions laws within the last 5 years; and
7. Neither the company seeking listing nor any of its subsidiaries or affiliates are currently identified as a party in pending litigation (including any administrative proceedings) involving the U.S. Department of Commerce.
Once the certifications above have been completed, an ITA industry specialist will review the application. This process can take several weeks to complete, and ITA personnel may reach out to the applicant's point of contact with questions or clarifications.
Companies will be notified of the results of the review process in advance of the publication of the RMIL. Before publication, ITA's industry specialists will work with each approved company to build out its profile on the RMIL, which may include details about the products and services the company offers as well as background or other information that the company chooses to include. ITA will publish the RMIL on its website once it has received and approved a minimum number of applications. ITA anticipates launching the first iteration of the listing in February 2027.
To ensure the RMIL remains accurate, ITA will ask all listed companies, via their designated point of contact, annually to certify that their information is up to date and confirm their desire to remain on the RMIL. Companies may request updates to their profiles on a rolling basis.

I. Executive Summary
A. Purpose
This proposed rule would update provisions related to Exchange eligibility and verification consistent with new requirements specified under section 71303 of
Public Law 119-21
(July 4, 2025), which we refer to as the Working Families Tax Cut (WFTC) legislation. We solicit input on ways Exchanges can strengthen certain verifications to promote program integrity while minimizing unnecessary or duplicative administrative burdens to the extent practicable. This proposed rule also contains related updates to provisions affecting inconsistency periods, enrollment options during inconsistency verification procedures, annual eligibility redeterminations and eligibility redeterminations during the plan year. It also expands enrollment methods during the verification process and establishes new effective dates.
